event_data.context:
## Expected workflow and state transitions

For every individual implementation-file or test-file edit, immediately run the smallest relevant test set. Record the durable workflow state as one of: `failing`, `passing-awaiting-lightweight-review-or-delivery`, `committed`, or `pushed` (or the delivery-mode-equivalent terminal checkpoint).

- `edit -> test -> failing`: do not commit or push. Permit only the next causal edit needed to address that failure, then test immediately again.
- `edit -> test -> passing`: stop implementation/test editing; complete mechanically required gates for that exact snapshot, perform a lightweight review aimed at catching obvious correctness, maintainability, test-quality, or production-risk mistakes, remediate and retest any finding, create a signed commit, run exact-commit verification, and make a normal push before another implementation/test edit where the configured delivery mode allows pushing.
- `passing -> lightweight-review finding -> failing-or-passing-awaiting-lightweight-review`: make only the causal remediation, retest immediately, and repeat the lightweight review before committing.
- `committed -> exact-revision verification failure`: do not push; make a new causal change and follow the normal signed-commit sequence. Never amend without explicit authorization.
- `pushed -> continuous-integration failure`: enter the existing Tiber-owned recovery hold and follow its single-causal-repair or authorized unchanged-revision-rerun policy before new feature work.
- `ticket implementation complete -> full review`: only when all planned increments are delivered and the agent is ready to call the ticket done, run the configured full multi-lens final review and its required clean iterations. Findings create a new causal edit/test/lightweight-review/commit/verify/push checkpoint; then reset and repeat the full final review as existing policy requires.
- interruption at any point: retain a durable checkpoint that identifies the exact snapshot and its last known state so another session can resume without guessing.

## Review boundaries

The lightweight checkpoint review and full ticket-completion review are distinct gates.

- The lightweight review occurs before every intermediate commit/push. Its bounded purpose is to catch obviously incorrect, unsafe, unmaintainable, or poorly tested changes without invoking the full coordinator, full lens set, or multi-iteration clean-review protocol.
- The full multi-lens final review does not run for each intermediate checkpoint. It runs once the complete ticket is otherwise ready to be declared done and retains all configured risk assessment, lens selection, fresh-reviewer, clean-iteration, reset, and durable-evidence requirements.
- A lightweight review cannot satisfy or reduce the final review requirement. Conversely, the final review must not be used to delay durable intermediate checkpoints.
- If the final review finds a defect, the remediation becomes a new normal checkpoint and is delivered before the full review restarts.

## Policy interactions

The feature belongs in `development-system:development-workflow` and must compose with, rather than replace, the existing test-driven-development, delivery, final-review, exact-revision verification, signing, continuous-integration recovery, authorization, and Tiber policies.

- Intermediate checkpoints require the lightweight review, signed commit, exact-commit gate, and normal push; they do not require the full multi-lens review.
- Full final review still precedes declaring the ticket complete. Any source remediation it causes follows the normal checkpoint sequence before final review restarts.
- Tiber remains the durable authority for active task state, ticket-completion review records when configured, interruption checkpoints, and pushed continuous-integration recovery holds.
- Delivery mode determines each checkpoint: direct-to-trunk uses a normal push; pull-request mode uses the repository’s branch/push and pull-request lifecycle without inferring permission to open, merge, amend, force-push, or delete; local-only mode stops at the locally permitted signed checkpoint and records that no push is authorized.
- Never infer authorization to amend commits, force-push, merge, delete remote state, open a pull request when permission is required, or bypass a protected delivery boundary.

## Bounded RED-to-GREEN exception

When a test edit and its corresponding implementation edit cannot independently pass, allow one explicitly declared and tightly scoped RED-to-GREEN pair. Test immediately after the RED edit, record the expected failure and its causal claim, make only the paired implementation edit, and test immediately again. If GREEN is not reached, return to the one-causal-edit loop. Once GREEN is reached, perform the lightweight review and checkpoint delivery immediately before any additional implementation or test change.

## Non-code and generated changes

Define explicit sequencing for documentation, configuration, formatting-only changes, and generated artifacts. Pure documentation or formatting changes may use their applicable deterministic gates instead of behavior tests, but independently passing snapshots still receive the lightweight review and checkpoint according to delivery mode. Configuration changes use checks that exercise the affected configuration. Generated artifacts remain coupled to the source edit that deterministically produces them and do not count as a convenience batch; regeneration and validation happen before the snapshot’s checkpoint. Mechanically required files or gates may join the snapshot only when they are consequences of the triggering edit.

## Tests

Add behavioral coverage for passing, failing, bounded RED-to-GREEN, interrupted/resumed, local-only, direct-to-trunk, and pull-request delivery modes. Tests must prove immediate test and lightweight-review ordering, prohibit convenience batching after GREEN, preserve authorization boundaries, and verify durable state transitions and recovery behavior. Add explicit coverage that intermediate commits do not trigger the full multi-lens review, while declaring the ticket done does require the full configured clean-iteration protocol and any final-review remediation is checkpointed before review restarts.

## Required instruction and skill changes

Update the development-workflow instructions and the retained test-driven-development and delivery workflow contracts as needed. Update final-review and Tiber instructions only where necessary to distinguish lightweight checkpoint review from terminal full-review sequencing and durable checkpoint records; do not duplicate their existing authorities. Add or update model-mediated behavior fixtures and graders because these instruction changes alter agent behavior, and bump the development-system plugin version and synchronized marketplace metadata under repository versioning policy.
event_data.summary: Development work can accumulate several independently passing changes before any durable checkpoint is created, making interruptions harder to recover from and increasing delivery risk. Introduce a workflow rule that tests every implementation or test edit immediately and preserves each passing snapshot through a lightweight pre-commit sanity review, signed commit, exact-commit verification, and delivery-mode-authorized push before further implementation or test edits. Keep the full multi-lens clean-iteration review as a ticket-completion gate only, immediately before the work is declared done.
event_data.title: Preserve each passing development step as a delivered checkpoint
